details.summary: This is an excellent, practical, and delicious meatless recipe that successfully leverages Greek yogurt and peas to hit a challenging protein target, while staying strictly within the required carbohydrate and saturated fat limits.

dimensions.feedback: The lemon, basil, pea, and ricotta flavor profile is classic and bright. The non-fat Greek yogurt adds tang that works well here. Tossing 2 cloves of raw minced garlic directly into the warm pasta might be slightly pungent; consider recommending grating or pasting the garlic so it melds into the sauce smoothly.
All ingredients are perfectly accounted for in the instructions and used in a logical order.
The instructions are very good and include the crucial time range and check step, but Step 2 is missing a doneness cue for the pasta. Add 'cook until al dente' or 'until tender with a slight bite'.
Highly aligned with Mediterranean cuisine, relying on staple flavors like lemon, basil, olive oil, and ricotta.
The cooking method is ideal. Adding the non-fat yogurt and ricotta off the heat and tossing with starchy pasta water is exactly the right technique to prevent the yogurt from splitting or curdling.
Computed macros are highly plausible and accurately reflect the weights of the pasta, peas, yogurt, and cheese.
The title and intro accurately describe the dish and its preparation. The tone is practical, food-focused, and completely free of disallowed diet or 'detox' language.
A highly appealing, comforting yet fresh weekday dinner. It cleverly uses Greek yogurt to create a 'creamy' sauce without heavy cream, which readers will appreciate.
Excellent crossover dish. It offers the comfort of creamy pasta while keeping saturated fat low for the liver (3.8 g) and relying on high-fiber whole grains and legumes for blood sugar stability.
Zero added sugars, and the carbohydrate component is high-quality (whole-wheat pasta and peas), fitting perfectly into the top end of the chapter's target window (53.7 g).

Fits the 'Vegetable & Meatless Dinners' chapter brilliantly. It successfully hits the challenging >=26 g meatless protein target (delivering 27.6 g) by thoughtfully combining Greek yogurt, peas, and a measured amount of cheese.
Easily achievable in roughly 20 minutes total from a cold start. The one-pot nature is practical, and all ingredients are standard supermarket items.
